expectations.text: Correctly identifies the co-author's reasoning as wrong — overlapping bootstrapped CIs do not imply the difference is not statistically significant
expectations.evidence: "Your co-author is applying a well-known statistical fallacy" and "Overlapping individual CIs do not imply non-significance of the difference. This is one of the most common misinterpretations in applied statistics."

expectations.text: Explains the logic: the CI for the difference between two statistics is not derived from the overlap of their individual CIs; they are separate quantities
expectations.evidence: "A 95% CI for a single estimate addresses: does this value differ from zero? It says nothing direct about whether two values differ from each other. To test the difference, you need a CI for the quantity (A − B), not for A and B separately."

expectations.text: Recommends the bootstrapped difference test (from bootnet, via differenceTest() or the plot method) as the correct tool for assessing pairwise centrality distinguishability
expectations.evidence: Provides full R workflow using bootnet's differenceTest() and plot method: "differenceTest(boot, x = 'A', y = 'B', measure = 'strength')" and "The visual plot of the difference matrix is equally informative"

expectations.text: Notes the practical implication: in most psychometric networks, few centrality pairs are statistically distinguishable; this is the expected finding, not evidence of a problem
